title: Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops
seoTitle: Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Thick chops, caramelized edges
description: Thick chops, caramelized edges. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Soy sauce, Garlic cloves, minced as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brine or season
steps.instruction: Pat pork dry. Salt 30 minutes ahead. Whisk glaze ingredients. Chops should be 1–1½ inches thick for even cooking. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill to 145°F
steps.instruction: Grill over medium-high 4–5 minutes per side until 140°F, then glaze and cook 1 minute per side until 145°F. Tenderloin: sear all sides, finish indirect to 145°F. Meat should spring back lightly.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Slice tenderloin on a bias. Hold chops on warm trays — pork dries out above 160°F, so don't overcook while waiting for the crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Glaze and hold
steps.instruction: Brush any remaining glaze over slices. Keep backup chops on a rack at 180°F — stacked pork steams and loses crust. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Slice cold protein thin for next-day wraps or salads — faster reheat, less dry-out.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Thick chops, caramelized edges. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Charcoal Grilled Pork Chops runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
